question:
A 61-year-old male patient reports experiencing recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and diarrhea
over the past year. He describes his stools as watery, frothy, and bulky, with some episodes occurring
without associated abdominal pain. Additionally, he mentions three episodes of intense flushing over
his head and neck without an identifiable cause. Physical examination reveals no significant
abnormalities. Further diagnostic evaluation confirms the presence of metastasized carcinoid tumors.

The physician discusses the condition with the patient and recommends long-term treatment with
octreotide. Which of the following conditions is most likely to occur as a side effect of this medication?
Answer Choices: (A) Hypocortisolism (B) Hypomagnesemia (C) Hypocalcemia (D) Hypophosphatemia
(E) Hypokalemia (F) Hypothyroidism (G) Hypogonadism (H) Hyperglycemia (I) Hyponatremia (J)
Hypoparathyroidism
 A. Hypokalemia
B. Hypocalcemia
C. Hypomagnesemia
D. Hypophosphatemia
E. Hypoparathyroidism
F. Hyponatremia
G. Hypocortisolism
H. Hypogonadism
I. Hyperglycemia
J. Hypothyroidism
